meta.timezone: Local wall-clock time, no UTC offset; converted from WHOOP UTC
meta.source: WHOOP API v2, 7 pulls merged, newest 2026-10-28.json
notes: One 'day' = one WHOOP physiological cycle, which starts when a main sleep starts. You often sleep late afternoon/evening, so two cycles can share a calendar date, and a cycle can run >30 h when only naps follow. Use cycle_start as the x-axis key.
total_sleep_h = main sleep + naps in that cycle (asleep time). sleep_consistency_pct is null while WHOOP was still calibrating (first 3 main sleeps reported 0).
For an ongoing cycle, recovery/RHR/HRV/SpO2/resp/sleep are final (scored at wake); only strain/steps/workouts are still accumulating.
Generated by build.py from the WHOOP pull + manual.json. Edit manual.json, not this file. Published for viewing only.

hr_zones.method: heart rate reserve (Karvonen), WHOOP's default: bpm = RHR + pct x (maxHR - RHR). Estimated with WHOOP max HR and 30-cycle median RHR; WHOOP's own cutoffs (in app settings) may differ slightly and recalibrate monthly.

vo2max_est._about: ESTIMATES from WHOOP data + profile, not a measurement. Compare with manual_logs.vo2max_lab once tested.

headline.basis: mean of the 3 methods; range = wider of the method spread or +/-5 (typical SEE)

methods.name: Uth-Sorensen heart rate ratio

inputs.hrmax_source: WHOOP max HR (not lab-measured; equals age-predicted)

methods.see: 2.7 ml/kg/min with measured HRmax, 4.7 with age-predicted HRmax (well-trained men 21-51)

source.label: Uth et al. 2004, Eur J Appl Physiol

inputs.par_basis: 42 min/wk of swim/row (WHOOP) avg of last 4 full weeks

source.label: Jackson et al. 1990, Med Sci Sports Exerc 22:863
Jurca et al. 2005, Am J Prev Med 29:185

sensitivity.note: Uth with highest HR seen in a workout (171); true max is at least this

not_used.reason: needs waist circumference (not measured yet) and a HUNT activity index

vo2max_est.series_method: Blended estimate (same 3-method mean as the headline) on the rolling 7-cycle mean RHR (>=3 cycles); activity rating and BMI held at current values, so only RHR moves the line. The latest point equals the headline.

hr_only.label: heart-rate method only (Uth-Sorensen)
hr_only.note: Reads higher than the blended headline; kept for comparison.

reference_bands._about: Reference categories for a man aged 41. Population/vendor figures from the cited source, NOT your data. Band rule: min inclusive, max exclusive, null = open-ended. build.py adds current (your value + window) and category. tone: good|ok|watch|flag for colouring. role 'reference_only' = shown for context, no goal attached.

source.label: Resting heart rate chart, men 36-45 (Top End Sports, general fitness chart)

hrv.label: HRV (RMSSD, overnight)

source.label: WHOOP member HRV by age and gender (age 40 middle 50% about 35-65 ms); ECG context: Lifelines men 40-44 median 29 ms, Nunan 2010 short-term RMSSD mean 42 (SD 15)

hrv.note: Typical lower/upper half split at 50 ms is the midpoint of WHOOP's 35-65 range, a display split, not a published cut.

source.label: WHOOP recovery colours (developer docs + The Locker); member average about 58%

WHOOP sleep consistency: member average 67.9%, aim for 80%+

WHOOP guidance, unofficial: Optimal 85%+, Sufficient 70-84%, Poor under 70%. WHOOP's own pages name the 85% and 70% levels (Sleep Planner 'perform' and 'get by') but no WHOOP support page with these tiers could be opened
Adult resting normal 12-20; most WHOOP members 13-18 during sleep

blood_pressure.label: Blood pressure

source.label: AHA/ACC 2025 high blood pressure guideline categories

blood_pressure.category_rule: worse of the systolic and diastolic categories (AHA: Elevated is systolic 120-129 with diastolic under 80)
blood_pressure.note: Your category is the worse of the two readings: e.g. 118/84 is Stage 1 because of the diastolic. Bars show systolic; diastolic bands are listed separately.

day_strain.label: Day strain

source.label: WHOOP strain levels: Light 0-9, Moderate 10-13, High 14-17, All out 18-21

day_strain.note: Not 'higher is better': the right band depends on that day's recovery colour.

weekly_cardio.label: Weekly cardio (moderate-equivalent minutes)

source.label: WHO 2020 physical activity guidelines: 150-300 min moderate or 75-150 min vigorous per week (1 vigorous min = 2 moderate) + strength 2+ days. Intensity from ACSM (Garber 2011): moderate 40-59% HRR (WHOOP zone 1), vigorous 60-89% HRR (zones 2-4+)

weekly_cardio.note: Moderate-equivalent = zone-1 minutes + 2 x zone 2-5 minutes, from all WHOOP-tracked workouts, full Mon-Sun weeks.

current.window: mean of last 4 full Mon-Sun weeks

goal.target: 150+ moderate-equivalent min every full week, plus strength 2+ days

steps.label: Steps

source.label: Paluch et al. 2022 meta-analysis: quartile medians 3,553 / 5,801 / 7,842 / 10,901; under-60 mortality benefit levels off at about 8,000-10,000

steps.note: WHOOP counts steps per cycle, and your cycles vary in length; swimming and rowing add fitness without steps.

bmi.label: BMI

source.label: WHO BMI classification (adults)

bmi.note: Informational only (you chose no weight goal). BMI can't tell muscle from fat; waist-to-height is your tracked body metric.

source.label: NICE NG246 (2025) central adiposity: 0.4-0.49 healthy, 0.5-0.59 increased risk, 0.6+ high risk

goal.target: Waist under 90 cm (waist-to-height under 0.5). No weight goal; BMI informational only

vo2max.label: VO2max (estimated)

source.label: The Cooper Institute, VO2max norms for men 40-49: Poor under 38.5, Fair 38.5-42.3, Good 42.4-46.3, Excellent 46.4-52.4, Superior 52.5+ (credit: The Cooper Institute)

estimate.method: Mean of three estimates from your own numbers: Uth-Sorensen heart-rate ratio (15.3 x max HR / resting HR), Jackson 1990 non-exercise model (age, BMI, activity rating) and Jurca 2005 non-exercise model (age, BMI, resting HR, activity rating). Typical error about +/-5 ml/kg/min; a lab test replaces it.

vo2max.note: Shows your lab result once one is logged; until then it shows the estimate (mean of 3 methods). The trend line uses the same 3-method blend, with only resting HR changing week to week.

current.window: estimated (mean of 3 methods), not a lab test

coach_copy._rules: Pick the first that applies: 1) an active manual_logs.status entry covering today -> status[flag]; 2) recovery_pct null -> pending; 3) recovery_pct < 34 -> red; 4) 34-66 -> amber; 5) >= 67 -> green.

recovery_day.title: Recovery day: swim easy, skip the erg
recovery_day.body: The erg will miss you, but it'll wait. Easy laps, long smooth exhales, then home to rest. Healing is training too.

rest_day.title: Rest day
rest_day.body: No pool, no erg, no guilt. Water, food, a long sleep. Tomorrow we pull.

sick.title: Off the clock: get well
sick.body: Today's only workout is rest. Fluids, easy food, sleep. The pool and the erg will be right there when you're back.

travel.title: On the road
travel.body: Find a pool or a rowing machine if you can; a brisk walk if you can't. Keep moving, keep it easy.

pending.title: Recovery's still cooking
pending.body: Your sleep hasn't scored yet. Check back once the strap syncs.

red.title: Row easy 30
red.body: Low battery today, so we keep it gentle: 30 minutes at an easy, conversational pace, or an easy swim. Skip the extras and chase a long sleep tonight.

amber.title: Plan as written
amber.body: Solid day to pull. Your 30-minute steady row is on, plus a swim if it's a pool day. Legs, back, arms; smooth and steady.

green.title: Green light: full plan
green.body: The body's ready. Swim, 30 steady minutes on the erg, then the weights. Stay smooth in zone 2; the engine grows when you cruise.
